cards.q: What are organic molecules?
cards.a: Molecules that contain carbon atoms (bonded to each other and usually to hydrogen).
cards.qAf: Wat is organiese molekules?
cards.aAf: Molekules wat koolstofatome bevat (aan mekaar gebind en gewoonlik aan waterstof).

cards.q: What is a hydrocarbon?
cards.a: An organic compound that consists of hydrogen and carbon atoms only.
cards.qAf: Wat is 'n koolwaterstof?
cards.aAf: 'n Organiese verbinding wat slegs uit waterstof- en koolstofatome bestaan.

cards.q: What is a functional group?
cards.a: A bond, atom or group of atoms that determines the physical and chemical properties of a group of organic compounds.
cards.qAf: Wat is 'n funksionele groep?
cards.aAf: 'n Binding, atoom of groep atome wat die fisiese en chemiese eienskappe van 'n groep organiese verbindings bepaal.

cards.q: What is a homologous series?
cards.a: A series of organic compounds with the same functional group and general formula, in which each member differs from the next by a CH₂ unit.
cards.qAf: Wat is 'n homoloë reeks?
cards.aAf: 'n Reeks organiese verbindings met dieselfde funksionele groep en algemene formule, waarin elke lid met 'n CH₂-eenheid van die volgende verskil.

cards.q: What is the difference between saturated and unsaturated compounds?
cards.a:
Saturated: only single bonds between carbon atoms (e.g. alkanes).
Unsaturated: at least one double or triple bond between carbon atoms (e.g. alkenes, alkynes).
cards.qAf: Wat is die verskil tussen versadigde en onversadigde verbindings?
cards.aAf:
Versadig: slegs enkelbindings tussen koolstofatome (bv. alkane).
Onversadig: ten minste een dubbel- of drievoudige binding tussen koolstofatome (bv. alkene, alkiene).

cards.q: Give the general formulae of alkanes, alkenes and alkynes.
cards.a:
Alkanes: CₙH₂ₙ₊₂
Alkenes: CₙH₂ₙ
Alkynes: CₙH₂ₙ₋₂
cards.qAf: Gee die algemene formules van alkane, alkene en alkiene.
cards.aAf:
Alkane: CₙH₂ₙ₊₂
Alkene: CₙH₂ₙ
Alkiene: CₙH₂ₙ₋₂

cards.q: What are structural isomers? Name the three types.
cards.a:
Compounds with the same molecular formula but different structural formulae.
Types: chain, positional and functional isomers.
cards.qAf: Wat is struktuurisomere? Noem die drie tipes.
cards.aAf:
Verbindings met dieselfde molekulêre formule maar verskillende struktuurformules.
Tipes: ketting-, posisie- en funksionele isomere.

cards.q: Give the functional group and name ending of alcohols, aldehydes and ketones.
cards.a:
Alcohol: hydroxyl group –OH, ending -ol.
Aldehyde: formyl group –CHO at the end of the chain, ending -al.
Ketone: carbonyl group C=O inside the chain, ending -one.
cards.qAf: Gee die funksionele groep en naamuitgang van alkohole, aldehiede en ketone.
cards.aAf:
Alkohol: hidroksielgroep –OH, uitgang -ol.
Aldehied: formielgroep –CHO aan die einde van die ketting, uitgang -al.
Ketoon: karbonielgroep C=O binne die ketting, uitgang -oon.

cards.q: Give the functional group and name ending of carboxylic acids and esters.
cards.a:
Carboxylic acid: carboxyl group –COOH, ending -oic acid.
Ester: –COO– linkage, ending -oate (e.g. ethyl ethanoate).
cards.qAf: Gee die funksionele groep en naamuitgang van karboksielsure en esters.
cards.aAf:
Karboksielsuur: karboksielgroep –COOH, uitgang -oësuur.
Ester: –COO–-koppeling, uitgang -oaat (bv. etieletanoaat).

cards.q: List the IUPAC stems for chains of 1 to 6 carbon atoms.
cards.a: 1 meth-, 2 eth-, 3 prop-, 4 but-, 5 pent-, 6 hex-
cards.qAf: Lys die IUPAC-stamme vir kettings van 1 tot 6 koolstofatome.
cards.aAf: 1 met-, 2 et-, 3 prop-, 4 but-, 5 pent-, 6 heks-

cards.q: How does chain length affect the boiling point in a homologous series?
cards.a: Longer chain → larger molecules with more surface area → stronger London (dispersion) forces → more energy needed to separate the molecules → higher boiling point.
cards.qAf: Hoe beïnvloed kettinglengte die kookpunt in 'n homoloë reeks?
cards.aAf: Langer ketting → groter molekules met meer oppervlakte → sterker London- (dispersie-) kragte → meer energie nodig om die molekules te skei → hoër kookpunt.

cards.q: How does branching affect the boiling point of isomers?
cards.a: More branching → more compact (spherical) molecules → smaller contact surface area → weaker intermolecular forces → lower boiling point.
cards.qAf: Hoe beïnvloed vertakking die kookpunt van isomere?
cards.aAf: Meer vertakking → meer kompakte (bolvormige) molekules → kleiner kontakoppervlakte → swakker intermolekulêre kragte → laer kookpunt.

cards.q: Why do alcohols have much higher boiling points than alkanes of similar size?
cards.a: Alcohols have hydrogen bonds between their molecules (from the –OH group), which are much stronger than the London forces between alkane molecules.
cards.qAf: Waarom het alkohole baie hoër kookpunte as alkane van soortgelyke grootte?
cards.aAf: Alkohole het waterstofbindings tussen hul molekules (van die –OH-groep), wat baie sterker is as die London-kragte tussen alkaanmolekules.

cards.q: How are vapour pressure and intermolecular forces related?
cards.a: Stronger intermolecular forces → fewer molecules escape to the gas phase → lower vapour pressure (and a higher boiling point).
cards.qAf: Hoe hou dampdruk en intermolekulêre kragte verband?
cards.aAf: Sterker intermolekulêre kragte → minder molekules ontsnap na die gasfase → laer dampdruk (en 'n hoër kookpunt).

cards.q: What is an addition reaction?
cards.a: A reaction in which atoms are added across the double (or triple) bond of an unsaturated compound. The double bond breaks and the product is saturated.
cards.qAf: Wat is 'n addisiereaksie?
cards.aAf: 'n Reaksie waarin atome oor die dubbel- (of drievoudige) binding van 'n onversadigde verbinding gevoeg word. Die dubbelbinding breek en die produk is versadig.

cards.q: Hydrogenation: reactants, conditions and product?
cards.a: Alkene + H₂, with a Ni or Pt catalyst (and heat) → alkane.
cards.qAf: Hidrogenering: reaktanse, toestande en produk?
cards.aAf: Alkeen + H₂, met 'n Ni- of Pt-katalisator (en hitte) → alkaan.

cards.q: Hydration: reactants, conditions and product?
cards.a: Alkene + H₂O, with an H₃PO₄ or H₂SO₄ catalyst and heat → alcohol.
cards.qAf: Hidrasie: reaktanse, toestande en produk?
cards.aAf: Alkeen + H₂O, met 'n H₃PO₄- of H₂SO₄-katalisator en hitte → alkohol.

cards.q: How do you test whether a hydrocarbon is unsaturated?
cards.a: Add bromine water. An alkene decolourises it quickly at room temperature (an addition reaction); an alkane does not.
cards.qAf: Hoe toets jy of 'n koolwaterstof onversadig is?
cards.aAf: Voeg broomwater by. 'n Alkeen ontkleur dit vinnig by kamertemperatuur ('n addisiereaksie); 'n alkaan nie.

cards.q: Dehydration of an alcohol: reaction type, conditions and products?
cards.a: Elimination. Alcohol heated with concentrated H₂SO₄ (or H₃PO₄) → alkene + H₂O.
cards.qAf: Dehidrasie van 'n alkohol: reaksietipe, toestande en produkte?
cards.aAf: Eliminasie. Alkohol verhit met gekonsentreerde H₂SO₄ (of H₃PO₄) → alkeen + H₂O.

cards.q: Dehydrohalogenation: reactants, conditions and products?
cards.a: Elimination. Haloalkane + concentrated KOH (or NaOH) dissolved in ethanol, heated strongly → alkene + KX + H₂O.
cards.qAf: Dehidrohalogenering: reaktanse, toestande en produkte?
cards.aAf: Eliminasie. Haloalkaan + gekonsentreerde KOH (of NaOH) opgelos in etanol, sterk verhit → alkeen + KX + H₂O.

cards.q: How is a haloalkane changed into an alcohol?
cards.a: Substitution (hydrolysis): haloalkane + dilute NaOH or KOH (aq), warmed gently → alcohol + NaX. The –OH replaces the halogen.
cards.qAf: Hoe word 'n haloalkaan na 'n alkohol omgeskakel?
cards.aAf: Substitusie (hidrolise): haloalkaan + verdunde NaOH of KOH (aq), effens verwarm → alkohol + NaX. Die –OH vervang die halogeen.

cards.q: How does an alkane react with a halogen?
cards.a: Substitution, in the presence of UV light (or heat): e.g. CH₄ + Cl₂ → CH₃Cl + HCl.
cards.qAf: Hoe reageer 'n alkaan met 'n halogeen?
cards.aAf: Substitusie, in die teenwoordigheid van UV-lig (of hitte): bv. CH₄ + Cl₂ → CH₃Cl + HCl.

cards.q: Esterification: reactants, conditions and products?
cards.a: Carboxylic acid + alcohol, heated with concentrated H₂SO₄ as catalyst → ester + water.
cards.qAf: Esterifikasie: reaktanse, toestande en produkte?
cards.aAf: Karboksielsuur + alkohol, verhit met gekonsentreerde H₂SO₄ as katalisator → ester + water.

cards.q: How is an ester named?
cards.a: The alcohol gives the first part (alkyl, e.g. ethyl) and the acid gives the second part with -oate (e.g. ethanoate): ethanol + ethanoic acid → ethyl ethanoate.
cards.qAf: Hoe word 'n ester benoem?
cards.aAf: Die alkohol gee die eerste deel (alkiel, bv. etiel) en die suur gee die tweede deel met -oaat (bv. etanoaat): etanol + etanoësuur → etieletanoaat.

cards.q: What is cracking, and what are its two types?
cards.a:
Breaking large alkane molecules into smaller, more useful alkanes and alkenes.
Thermal cracking: high temperature and pressure, no catalyst.
Catalytic cracking: lower temperature with a catalyst (e.g. zeolite).
cards.qAf: Wat is kraking, en wat is die twee tipes?
cards.aAf:
Die opbreek van groot alkaanmolekules in kleiner, nuttiger alkane en alkene.
Termiese kraking: hoë temperatuur en druk, geen katalisator.
Katalitiese kraking: laer temperatuur met 'n katalisator (bv. zeoliet).

cards.q: What are the products of complete and incomplete combustion of an alkane?
cards.a:
Complete (excess O₂): CO₂ + H₂O.
Incomplete (limited O₂): CO and/or C (soot) + H₂O.
cards.qAf: Wat is die produkte van volledige en onvolledige verbranding van 'n alkaan?
cards.aAf:
Volledig (oormaat O₂): CO₂ + H₂O.
Onvolledig (beperkte O₂): CO en/of C (roet) + H₂O.

cards.q: What is the difference between addition and condensation polymerisation?
cards.a:
Addition: unsaturated monomers (alkenes) join and no other product forms (e.g. polyethene).
Condensation: monomers with two functional groups join and a small molecule such as water is released each time (e.g. polyester, nylon).
cards.qAf: Wat is die verskil tussen addisie- en kondensasiepolimerisasie?
cards.aAf:
Addisie: onversadigde monomere (alkene) verbind en geen ander produk vorm nie (bv. poliëteen).
Kondensasie: monomere met twee funksionele groepe verbind en 'n klein molekule soos water word elke keer vrygestel (bv. poliëster, nylon).

cards.q: Define an acid and a base according to Brønsted–Lowry.
cards.a:
Acid: a proton (H⁺) donor.
Base: a proton (H⁺) acceptor.
cards.qAf: Definieer 'n suur en 'n basis volgens Brønsted-Lowry.
cards.aAf:
Suur: 'n proton- (H⁺-) skenker.
Basis: 'n proton- (H⁺-) aanvaarder.

cards.q: What is a conjugate acid–base pair?
cards.a: Two substances that differ by one proton (H⁺), e.g. HCl / Cl⁻ and H₃O⁺ / H₂O.
cards.qAf: Wat is 'n gekonjugeerde suur-basis-paar?
cards.aAf: Twee stowwe wat met een proton (H⁺) verskil, bv. HCl / Cl⁻ en H₃O⁺ / H₂O.

cards.q: What is an ampholyte? Give an example.
cards.a: A substance that can act as either an acid or a base, e.g. H₂O, HCO₃⁻ or HSO₄⁻.
cards.qAf: Wat is 'n amfoliet? Gee 'n voorbeeld.
cards.aAf: 'n Stof wat óf as 'n suur óf as 'n basis kan optree, bv. H₂O, HCO₃⁻ of HSO₄⁻.

cards.q: What is the difference between a strong and a weak acid?
cards.a: A strong acid ionises completely in water (e.g. HCl, H₂SO₄, HNO₃). A weak acid ionises only partially (e.g. CH₃COOH, H₂CO₃) and has a small Ka.
cards.qAf: Wat is die verskil tussen 'n sterk en 'n swak suur?
cards.aAf: 'n Sterk suur ioniseer volledig in water (bv. HCl, H₂SO₄, HNO₃). 'n Swak suur ioniseer slegs gedeeltelik (bv. CH₃COOH, H₂CO₃) en het 'n klein Ka.

cards.q: Is a concentrated acid the same as a strong acid?
cards.a: No. Concentrated/dilute describes how much acid is dissolved per volume. Strong/weak describes how completely it ionises.
cards.qAf: Is 'n gekonsentreerde suur dieselfde as 'n sterk suur?
cards.aAf: Nee. Gekonsentreerd/verdund beskryf hoeveel suur per volume opgelos is. Sterk/swak beskryf hoe volledig dit ioniseer.

cards.q: What is Kw, and what is its value at 25 °C?
cards.a: The ionisation constant of water: Kw = [H₃O⁺][OH⁻] = 1 × 10⁻¹⁴ at 25 °C.
cards.qAf: Wat is Kw, en wat is die waarde daarvan by 25 °C?
cards.aAf: Die ionisasiekonstante van water: Kw = [H₃O⁺][OH⁻] = 1 × 10⁻¹⁴ by 25 °C.

cards.q: How do you calculate pH?
cards.a: pH = −log[H₃O⁺]. pH < 7 is acidic, 7 is neutral and > 7 is basic (at 25 °C).
cards.qAf: Hoe bereken jy pH?
cards.aAf: pH = −log[H₃O⁺]. pH < 7 is suur, 7 is neutraal en > 7 is basies (by 25 °C).

cards.q: What is the difference between the equivalence point and the endpoint of a titration?
cards.a:
Equivalence point: the acid and base have reacted completely in the mole ratio of the equation.
Endpoint: the point where the indicator changes colour.
cards.qAf: Wat is die verskil tussen die ekwivalensiepunt en die eindpunt van 'n titrasie?
cards.aAf:
Ekwivalensiepunt: die suur en basis het volledig in die molverhouding van die vergelyking gereageer.
Eindpunt: die punt waar die indikator van kleur verander.

cards.q: Which indicator do you choose for each type of titration?
cards.a:
Strong acid + strong base: bromothymol blue (equivalence point ≈ pH 7).
Weak acid + strong base: phenolphthalein (pH > 7).
Strong acid + weak base: methyl orange (pH < 7).
cards.qAf: Watter indikator kies jy vir elke tipe titrasie?
cards.aAf:
Sterk suur + sterk basis: broomtimolblou (ekwivalensiepunt ≈ pH 7).
Swak suur + sterk basis: fenolftaleïen (pH > 7).
Sterk suur + swak basis: metieloranje (pH < 7).

cards.q: Which formula links the concentrations and volumes in a titration?
cards.a: (ca × Va) / (cb × Vb) = na / nb, where na : nb is the mole ratio from the balanced equation.
cards.qAf: Watter formule verbind die konsentrasies en volumes in 'n titrasie?
cards.aAf: (ca × Va) / (cb × Vb) = na / nb, waar na : nb die molverhouding uit die gebalanseerde vergelyking is.

cards.q: What is hydrolysis of a salt? Is a sodium ethanoate solution acidic or basic?
cards.a: The reaction of a salt (its ions) with water. CH₃COO⁻ reacts with water to form OH⁻, so a sodium ethanoate solution is basic. (NH₄Cl gives an acidic solution.)
cards.qAf: Wat is hidrolise van 'n sout? Is 'n natriumetanoaat-oplossing suur of basies?
cards.aAf: Die reaksie van 'n sout (sy ione) met water. CH₃COO⁻ reageer met water om OH⁻ te vorm, dus is 'n natriumetanoaat-oplossing basies. (NH₄Cl gee 'n suur oplossing.)

cards.q: What is a buffer solution?
cards.a: A solution that resists changes in pH when small amounts of acid or base are added. It contains a weak acid and its conjugate base (or a weak base and its conjugate acid).
cards.qAf: Wat is 'n bufferoplossing?
cards.aAf: 'n Oplossing wat veranderinge in pH weerstaan wanneer klein hoeveelhede suur of basis bygevoeg word. Dit bevat 'n swak suur en sy gekonjugeerde basis (of 'n swak basis en sy gekonjugeerde suur).

cards.q: Define oxidation and reduction in terms of electrons.
cards.a:
Oxidation: loss of electrons (oxidation number increases).
Reduction: gain of electrons (oxidation number decreases).
cards.qAf: Definieer oksidasie en reduksie in terme van elektrone.
cards.aAf:
Oksidasie: verlies van elektrone (oksidasiegetal neem toe).
Reduksie: opname van elektrone (oksidasiegetal neem af).

cards.q: What are an oxidising agent and a reducing agent?
cards.a:
Oxidising agent: accepts electrons, so it is reduced.
Reducing agent: donates electrons, so it is oxidised.
cards.qAf: Wat is 'n oksideermiddel en 'n reduseermiddel?
cards.aAf:
Oksideermiddel: neem elektrone op, dus word dit gereduseer.
Reduseermiddel: staan elektrone af, dus word dit geoksideer.

cards.q: At which electrode does oxidation take place, and at which reduction?
cards.a: Oxidation always happens at the anode and reduction at the cathode (in both galvanic and electrolytic cells). Memory aid: AN OX, RED CAT.
cards.qAf: By watter elektrode vind oksidasie plaas, en by watter reduksie?
cards.aAf: Oksidasie vind altyd by die anode plaas en reduksie by die katode (in galvaniese én elektrolitiese selle). Geheuehulp: AN OX, RED CAT.

cards.q: Compare a galvanic cell and an electrolytic cell.
cards.a:
Galvanic: a spontaneous reaction converts chemical energy → electrical energy. Anode is negative.
Electrolytic: a power supply drives a non-spontaneous reaction, electrical energy → chemical energy. Anode is positive.
cards.qAf: Vergelyk 'n galvaniese sel en 'n elektrolitiese sel.
cards.aAf:
Galvanies: 'n spontane reaksie skakel chemiese energie → elektriese energie om. Anode is negatief.
Elektrolities: 'n kragbron dryf 'n nie-spontane reaksie aan, elektriese energie → chemiese energie. Anode is positief.

cards.q: What are the functions of the salt bridge?
cards.a: It completes the circuit and lets ions move between the half-cells, which keeps each half-cell electrically neutral.
cards.qAf: Wat is die funksies van die soutbrug?
cards.aAf: Dit voltooi die stroombaan en laat ione tussen die halfselle beweeg, wat elke halfsel elektries neutraal hou.

cards.q: What are standard conditions for electrochemical cells?
cards.a: Temperature 25 °C (298 K), concentration 1 mol·dm⁻³ and pressure 1 atm (101.3 kPa).
cards.qAf: Wat is standaardtoestande vir elektrochemiese selle?
cards.aAf: Temperatuur 25 °C (298 K), konsentrasie 1 mol·dm⁻³ en druk 1 atm (101,3 kPa).

cards.q: How do you calculate the standard emf of a cell, and how do you know the reaction is spontaneous?
cards.a: E°cell = E°cathode − E°anode (use reduction potentials from the table). A positive E°cell means the reaction is spontaneous.
cards.qAf: Hoe bereken jy die standaard-EMK van 'n sel, en hoe weet jy die reaksie is spontaan?
cards.aAf: E°sel = E°katode − E°anode (gebruik reduksiepotensiale uit die tabel). 'n Positiewe E°sel beteken die reaksie is spontaan.

cards.q: What is the standard hydrogen electrode used for?
cards.a: It is the reference half-cell (E° = 0.00 V) against which all standard electrode potentials are measured: a Pt electrode in 1 mol·dm⁻³ H⁺ with H₂ gas at 1 atm, 25 °C.
cards.qAf: Waarvoor word die standaard-waterstofelektrode gebruik?
cards.aAf: Dit is die verwysingshalfsel (E° = 0,00 V) waarteen alle standaard-elektrodepotensiale gemeet word: 'n Pt-elektrode in 1 mol·dm⁻³ H⁺ met H₂-gas by 1 atm, 25 °C.

cards.q: Write the cell notation for the Zn–Cu (Daniell) cell.
cards.a:
Zn(s) | Zn²⁺(aq) || Cu²⁺(aq) | Cu(s)
Anode on the left, cathode on the right, || is the salt bridge.
cards.qAf: Skryf die selnotasie vir die Zn–Cu (Daniell-) sel.
cards.aAf:
Zn(s) | Zn²⁺(aq) || Cu²⁺(aq) | Cu(s)
Anode links, katode regs, || is die soutbrug.

cards.q: In which direction do electrons flow in the external circuit of a galvanic cell?
cards.a: From the anode (where oxidation releases electrons) to the cathode.
cards.qAf: In watter rigting vloei elektrone in die eksterne stroombaan van 'n galvaniese sel?
cards.aAf: Van die anode (waar oksidasie elektrone vrystel) na die katode.

cards.q: How is a spoon electroplated with silver?
cards.a: The spoon is the cathode, a silver bar is the anode and the electrolyte is a silver salt solution (e.g. AgNO₃). At the cathode: Ag⁺ + e⁻ → Ag.
cards.qAf: Hoe word 'n lepel met silwer geëlektroplateer?
cards.aAf: Die lepel is die katode, 'n silwerstaaf is die anode en die elektroliet is 'n silwersoutoplossing (bv. AgNO₃). By die katode: Ag⁺ + e⁻ → Ag.

cards.q: How is impure copper refined by electrolysis?
cards.a: Impure copper is the anode, pure copper is the cathode and CuSO₄ solution is the electrolyte. Cu dissolves at the anode and deposits as pure Cu at the cathode; impurities fall as sludge.
cards.qAf: Hoe word onsuiwer koper deur elektrolise gesuiwer?
cards.aAf: Onsuiwer koper is die anode, suiwer koper is die katode en CuSO₄-oplossing is die elektroliet. Cu los by die anode op en word as suiwer Cu by die katode neergelê; onsuiwerhede val as slyk uit.

cards.q: Name the three primary nutrients that plants need from fertilisers.
cards.a: Nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P) and potassium (K).
cards.qAf: Noem die drie primêre voedingstowwe wat plante uit kunsmis nodig het.
cards.aAf: Stikstof (N), fosfor (P) en kalium (K).

cards.q: Write the equation and conditions for the Haber process.
cards.a:
N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g), ΔH < 0
Iron catalyst, about 450 °C and 150–200 atm.
cards.qAf: Skryf die vergelyking en toestande vir die Haber-proses.
cards.aAf:
N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g), ΔH < 0
Ysterkatalisator, ongeveer 450 °C en 150–200 atm.

cards.q: Where do the raw materials for the Haber process come from?
cards.a:
N₂: fractional distillation of liquid air.
H₂: natural gas (methane) by steam reforming, or from coal.
cards.qAf: Waar kom die grondstowwe vir die Haber-proses vandaan?
cards.aAf:
N₂: fraksionele distillasie van vloeibare lug.
H₂: aardgas (metaan) deur stoomhervorming, of uit steenkool.

cards.q: Why is about 450 °C used in the Haber process when a lower temperature gives a better yield?
cards.a: The forward reaction is exothermic, so a low temperature favours NH₃, but then the rate is too slow. 450 °C with a catalyst is a compromise between yield and rate.
cards.qAf: Waarom word ongeveer 450 °C in die Haber-proses gebruik as 'n laer temperatuur 'n beter opbrengs gee?
cards.aAf: Die voorwaartse reaksie is eksotermies, dus bevoordeel 'n lae temperatuur NH₃, maar dan is die tempo te stadig. 450 °C met 'n katalisator is 'n kompromie tussen opbrengs en tempo.

cards.q: Why does a high pressure increase the yield of ammonia?
cards.a: There are 4 mol of gas on the left and 2 mol on the right. Higher pressure favours the side with fewer moles of gas, so the equilibrium shifts towards NH₃.
cards.qAf: Waarom verhoog 'n hoë druk die opbrengs van ammoniak?
cards.aAf: Daar is 4 mol gas aan die linkerkant en 2 mol aan die regterkant. Hoër druk bevoordeel die kant met minder mol gas, dus skuif die ewewig na NH₃.

cards.q: Does a catalyst increase the yield of ammonia?
cards.a: No. A catalyst increases the rate of both the forward and reverse reactions equally, so equilibrium is reached faster, but the yield (and Kc) stays the same.
cards.qAf: Verhoog 'n katalisator die opbrengs van ammoniak?
cards.aAf: Nee. 'n Katalisator verhoog die tempo van die voorwaartse en terugwaartse reaksies ewe veel, dus word ewewig vinniger bereik, maar die opbrengs (en Kc) bly dieselfde.

cards.q: List the steps of the Contact process.
cards.a:
1. S + O₂ → SO₂
2. 2SO₂ + O₂ ⇌ 2SO₃ (V₂O₅ catalyst, about 450 °C)
3. SO₃ + H₂SO₄ → H₂S₂O₇ (oleum)
4. H₂S₂O₇ + H₂O → 2H₂SO₄
cards.qAf: Lys die stappe van die Kontakproses.
cards.aAf:
1. S + O₂ → SO₂
2. 2SO₂ + O₂ ⇌ 2SO₃ (V₂O₅-katalisator, ongeveer 450 °C)
3. SO₃ + H₂SO₄ → H₂S₂O₇ (oleum)
4. H₂S₂O₇ + H₂O → 2H₂SO₄

cards.q: Why is SO₃ not dissolved directly in water in the Contact process?
cards.a: The reaction is so exothermic that it forms a mist of sulfuric acid droplets that is hard to collect. SO₃ is dissolved in concentrated H₂SO₄ instead to form oleum.
cards.qAf: Waarom word SO₃ nie direk in water opgelos in die Kontakproses nie?
cards.aAf: Die reaksie is so eksotermies dat dit 'n mis van swawelsuurdruppels vorm wat moeilik is om op te vang. SO₃ word eerder in gekonsentreerde H₂SO₄ opgelos om oleum te vorm.

cards.q: What is the Ostwald process used for?
cards.a: Making nitric acid from ammonia: NH₃ → NO → NO₂ → HNO₃ (Pt catalyst in the first step).
cards.qAf: Waarvoor word die Ostwald-proses gebruik?
cards.aAf: Om salpetersuur uit ammoniak te maak: NH₃ → NO → NO₂ → HNO₃ (Pt-katalisator in die eerste stap).

cards.q: Name three fertilisers and how they are made.
cards.a:
Ammonium nitrate: NH₃ + HNO₃.
Ammonium sulfate: NH₃ + H₂SO₄.
Superphosphate: phosphate rock + H₂SO₄.
cards.qAf: Noem drie kunsmisstowwe en hoe hulle gemaak word.
cards.aAf:
Ammoniumnitraat: NH₃ + HNO₃.
Ammoniumsulfaat: NH₃ + H₂SO₄.
Superfosfaat: fosfaatrots + H₂SO₄.

cards.q: What does '3 : 2 : 1 (25)' on a fertiliser bag mean?
cards.a: N : P : K is in the ratio 3 : 2 : 1, and these three nutrients make up 25% of the mass of the fertiliser.
cards.qAf: Wat beteken '3 : 2 : 1 (25)' op 'n kunsmissak?
cards.aAf: N : P : K is in die verhouding 3 : 2 : 1, en hierdie drie voedingstowwe maak 25% van die massa van die kunsmis uit.

cards.q: What is eutrophication?
cards.a: Excess fertiliser washes into water, causing an algal bloom. When the algae die, decomposing bacteria use up the dissolved oxygen, and fish and other aquatic life die.
cards.qAf: Wat is eutrofikasie?
cards.aAf: Oortollige kunsmis spoel in water in en veroorsaak 'n algeblom. Wanneer die alge doodgaan, gebruik ontbindende bakterieë die opgeloste suurstof op, en visse en ander waterlewe vrek.
